goal: Basic conversation at a dinner table (a meal with a Hà Nội family or friends) and understanding basic street talk (sellers, waiters, drivers, neighbours) in Northern Vietnamese. Vocabulary keeps growing, and from issue 6 every issue also teaches one sentence frame and one short dialogue built from known words, alternating between the table and the street (the learner set this goal on 2026-11-22; see docs/PEDAGOGY.md, Conversation).

phases.title: Core vocabulary, with talk woven in
phases.target: About 300 words recognised by ear and recalled by meaning (meaning strength 0.8 or more), with a frame and a dialogue in every issue from issue 6.
phases.exit: Move on when about 250 words are in the review deck or on the known list and recent meaning strength averages 0.8 or more.

phases.title: Sentence frames (woven into every issue)
phases.target: Twenty high-value frames for the table and the street, one per issue, each coming back on an expanding schedule: Mời ... ăn cơm, ... nữa không?, Tôi muốn ..., ... ở đâu?, Có ... không?, Cho tôi ..., ... bao nhiêu tiền?, ... được không?, Anh/chị là người ...?, Tôi không ...
phases.exit: The learner builds and understands each pattern with known words at 0.8 or more.

phases.title: Conversation (woven in, then longer)
phases.target: Short dialogues in every issue, alternating a meal with a family and the street (market, café, xe ôm, asking the way, neighbours); every five or six issues a longer consolidation dialogue that recombines the recent frames.

units.title: Food and drink
units.notes: The learner already knew almost all of it; only gà, cá and bò needed practice. The other nine are on the known list. Issue story: "Younger than the Eiffel Tower" (phở, bánh mì, coffee, egg coffee).

units.title: Big numbers and prices
units.notes: Numbers 0 to 10 are a warm-up only. Brings in the nặng and ngã tones (triệu, chục, nữa, rưỡi) that lesson 1 lacked, and the hỏi and ngã contrast (nửa and nữa, rẻ and rẽ). Issue story: "Copper, paper, plastic" (the đồng, coins abandoned in 2011, polymer notes, Đồng Xuân market, Thăng Long 1010). Played on 2026-11-21 (iPhone, old battle version): 64% first try, 30 minutes, Too hard; listening strong, typing weak; numbers 1 to 10 not secure.

units.title: One to ten, properly
units.notes: The learner asked to learn 1 to 10 properly and for real-life use. Story: Sơn Tinh and Thủy Tinh, the bride price of nines. Real-life price listening. Review of the most confused issue 2 words. Played on 2026-11-21 (Mac): 81% first try, merit, 17.6 minutes, Just right, fun Good, story Skipped it. Real life 5 of 8: missed a fare of sáu mươi nghìn (typed 231000), a bill of 105,000 (typed 10000) and a tourist price. Asked for more illustrations; skips the did-you-know pop-ups.

units.title: People and family
units.notes: Taught as the words you call people by (there is no all-purpose you): tên, tôi, anh, chị, em, cô, chú, ông, bà, bạn. Hà Nội says bố and mẹ (the South says ba and má). Story: "A country of Nguyễns" (31.5% are Nguyễn; called by the given name with a family word; why so many: 1232, 1407, 1592; ông trẻ; the 1841 exile; Nguyen in Iceland). Real life keeps practising prices by ear. Left for later: bác (its gloss overlaps cô and chú), con, cháu, vợ, chồng, gia đình, người, bố, mẹ.
units.storyIdea: Who you call anh, chị or em: how the family system of address works, and the family altar in Hà Nội homes.

units.title: At the market: prices as sellers say them
units.notes: Next, at the learner's request after issue 4: "someone telling me a price and me understanding what it is", noting that sellers usually drop nghìn ("mười" for 10,000) and shorten hundreds. Teach the spoken forms Hà Nội sellers really use (dropped nghìn, hai lăm for 25, trăm rưỡi for 150 and similar), each one confirmed by the Vietnamese reviewer before it is taught, alongside the market words. Consolidates the weakest words: trăm, nghìn, mươi, lăm, rưỡi, triệu. Real-life prices are the weakest skill (60% right, about 27 seconds an answer). quả and thịt lợn are Northern (the South says trái and thịt heo). Keep it to about 45 answers. Issue 5 (2026-11-22): mua, quả, cam, chuối, cân, thịt, bớt, hết; review trăm, rưỡi, lăm, đắt. Spoken price forms taught: nghìn dropped (ba mươi = 30.000₫), mươi dropped before a last digit (hai lăm, ba lăm, bốn lăm), trăm plus a digit for tens (trăm hai = 120.000₫, trăm tám = 180.000₫), trăm rưỡi and hai trăm rưỡi; all awaiting the Vietnamese reviewer. Story: the Tết fruit tray (bananas in the North, puns in the South), vải thiều and cụ Cơm, shoulder-pole sellers, cốm. Left for later: chục for tens (hai chục = 20.000₫, a near-synonym of mươi), lạng (100 g), triệu hai and triệu rưỡi, xoài, dưa hấu, trứng, túi, chợ, bán. Played on 2026-11-22 (Mac): 87% first try, merit, 13.3 minutes, Just right, fun Good, story OK; hardest quả, bớt, hết. Real life 4 of 8: ba lăm picked as 53.000₫, trăm hai as 102.000₫, chuối hai mươi một nải as 21.000₫, and Cho anh mười cân cam for one kilo (một against mười); trăm rưỡi, bốn lăm (typed) and hai trăm rưỡi were right. Typing: bớt came out as dat (đắt), quả as cam. The review that night (91%) heard bớt as hết and đồng as cân.
units.storyIdea: Fruit of the North through the seasons, and street vendors with their shoulder poles (quang gánh).

units.title: At the table: a meal with a Hà Nội family
frames: Mời ... ăn cơm (inviting everyone to start, oldest first): taught in issue 6; brought back in issue 7 (a phở seller: Mời anh vào ăn phở ạ!); bring back about issue 9 or 10, and about issue 13
... nữa nhé? / ... nữa không? (offering more): heard in issue 6 (Cháu ăn bát nữa nhé?); teach as a frame at the next table issue
Cháu no rồi ạ. (I'm full): taught as a chunk in issue 6; bring back with the frame
dialogueIdeas: Bà offers more rice; you are full
Inviting the elders to start the meal
units.notes: The learner's goal is dinner-table conversation. Verify every custom and phrase with the Vietnamese reviewer (Northern usage: vâng for yes; who invites whom). Issue 6 (2026-11-22): mời, cháu, bát, đũa, canh, no, vâng, with a warm-up of ăn, uống and cảm ơn; review bớt, nữa, lăm, quả. Frame: Mời ... ăn cơm (Cháu mời ông ăn cơm ạ; Mời cả nhà ăn cơm; Cháu mời chú uống trà ạ). Chunks: Cháu no rồi ạ., Vâng, ngon quá ạ!, Vâng, cháu cảm ơn bà ạ. Dialogue at Minh's grandparents' table, ending on being full; real life rehearses the issue 5 price traps (bốn lăm against 54, trăm sáu against 106 and 600, a price followed by một quả or một chai, một against mười) on the way to dinner. Story: "Words before chopsticks" (the mâm cơm, the shared fish-sauce bowl, Ăn trông nồi ngồi trông hướng, chopstick rules, Lời chào cao hơn mâm cỗ). Left for later: thêm (near-synonym of nữa), đói (antonym of no; the describing unit), nước mắm and chấm as words, mâm, ừ, xơi, gắp, mời ... uống nước as its own frame. Played on 2026-11-23 (iPhone): 88% first try, merit, Too hard, fun OK, story OK (6 seconds on the opening); hardest mời, đũa, canh, bớt. Conversation check right. Real life 5 of 8, every miss a price trap: Của anh hết trăm ba typed as 300 (trăm ba read as ba trăm), Bưởi bốn mươi một quả picked as 41.000₫ (the second issue running for the X mươi | một [unit] parse), and Anh lấy mấy quả ạ? answered with một cân. bớt 0 by meaning (heard as mời). The review that afternoon scored 69% (bớt typed as dat again, bạn as bat, tên as tien).
units.storyIdea: The Northern family meal: the shared tray (mâm cơm) and the custom of inviting each elder to eat before you start.

units.title: Getting around
units.notes: rẽ was a contrast word in lesson 2 (rẻ against rẽ). Issue 7 (2026-11-23), made easier after issue 6 was rated Too hard: six words (xe ôm, đâu, trái, gần, rẽ, phải), warm-up đi, ăn, uống, review bớt, mời, đắt, 42 answers. Frame Đi ... bao nhiêu? with a xe ôm dialogue (agree the fare, bargain, left or right). The two persistent price traps are taught once in combos (trăm ba against ba trăm; bốn mươi, một quả as 40.000₫ each) and kept out of real life, whose six prices use forms the learner got right before (ba mươi, hai trăm rưỡi, hai lăm, ba lăm, trăm rưỡi, mười nghìn in full). Story: "The bridge that keeps left" (Long Biên: the 1899 – 1902 Daydé & Pillé plate, not Eiffel, the 1953 decree to keep left, the war, today). Left for later: xa (in a note), đây, thẳng (đi thẳng), dừng, xuống (Cho anh xuống đây), tắc đường, xe máy, ô tô, xe buýt, đường, ngã tư. Played on 2026-11-24 (iPhone): 72% first try, merit, 20.9 minutes, Too hard, fun Boring, story OK; hardest gần, phải, bớt, đắt (the short new words confused with each other by meaning); Cà phê trứng ba lăm heard as 25.000₫. Asked for a clear rule for lăm, rưỡi and năm, and an article tied to the lesson, so issue 8 is a numbers clinic; xa, thẳng, dừng and the rest wait for a later street issue.
units.storyIdea: Millions of motorbikes, the Long Biên bridge, and how to cross a Hà Nội street.
frames: Đi ... bao nhiêu? (how much to ...?, agreeing a fare with a xe ôm or taxi): taught in issue 7; brought back in issue 8 (Đi Hồ Tây bao nhiêu em?, in a real-life prompt, answered hai nhăm); bring back about issue 10 and about issue 14
Rẽ trái / rẽ phải (steering a driver): chunks in issue 7

units.title: A numbers clinic: the forms in spoken prices
units.notes: A one-issue clinic after issues 6 and 7 were both rated Too hard (issue 7 also Boring), answering the learner's request of 2026-11-24: "I need to understand better prices, like when to use lam or rau or nam for example" (rau is almost certainly rưỡi). Four new words, each a form with one rule: nhăm (five after the tens, Hà Nội), mốt (one after the tens from 20), tư (four after the tens from 20), chục (a ten, as sellers count); review lăm, rưỡi, năm, mươi, trăm (heard, not typed). One grammar note sets out năm, lăm or nhăm; một or mốt; bốn or tư; mười, mươi or chục; and rưỡi as half the unit before it. 33 answers before rush hour. Story: a morning at Đồng Xuân market, each beat a stall with a price in one form and one sourced fact about numbers or money. Done when published: the forms come back in every later price line, not as a unit of their own. Left for later: lạng (100 g), triệu rưỡi and triệu hai, trăm plus a digit (trăm hai, trăm mốt) as a rule of its own.
frames: Đi ... bao nhiêu? brought back once (a real-life prompt)

units.title: At the market, you do the talking
units.notes: Review of 2026-11-24: fun fell to Boring twice and the learner asked to say prices, not only understand them. The learner makes counter-offers (... được không?) and says prices in Say the price questions, with the seller answering back and a running total haggled off. Brings back bớt, đắt, chục (leeches) and the 'X mươi, một [unit]' price, said rather than heard. Story tied to the market: the old quarter's Hàng streets, each named for the goods once sold there, if the sources support it. Issue 9 (2026-11-24): hàng, được, lấy, trứng; frame ... được không?; three Say the price counter-offers with seller replies and a haggled-off total; story of the Hàng streets; new cover oldQuarter.

units.title: Greetings and small talk (street)
units.notes: ạ at the end of a sentence to older people; vâng is the typical Northern polite yes. After issue 4: add cháu and con, what you call yourself to cô, chú, ông and bà (Cháu chào bà ạ). Reshaped for the street half of the goal: greeting neighbours and sellers, where are you from, see you again. Table manners (mời, vâng, ạ) move to the table unit. Issue 10 (2026-11-25): chào, biết, khỏe, xin lỗi, gặp, one per tone, with the story of the tone marks; the learner asked for something other than prices after issue 9 and for help remembering tones. Bring prices and đắt back in issue 11.
units.storyIdea: Hà Nội manners: vâng and ạ, greeting elders first, and the Temple of Literature (Văn Miếu, 1070), the first university.

units.title: Everyday verbs
units.notes: Likely partly known: use a warm-up for ăn, uống, đi, có, là. Verbs unlock the patterns phase. Review 2026-11-26: keep issue 11's recipe (four picturable words, a short frame to say, reaction lines, a winnable dialogue check). Verbs to act out fit: ăn, uống, đi are already taught, so pick visible actions (ngủ, xem, nghe, nói, mua is taught) and a frame like Cháu muốn ... (I want to ...).
units.storyIdea: A day in Hà Nội: morning exercise around Hoàn Kiếm Lake at dawn, and the legend of the returned sword.

units.title: Describing words
units.notes: rét is the Northern word for cold weather (lạnh also works). Describing words follow the noun. Issue 11 (2026-11-26): nóng, rét, đẹp, đói with ... quá!, after issue 10 (abstract greetings) was Too hard and Boring. Later describing words (to, nhỏ, mệt, mới, cũ) can come back in a later issue.
units.storyIdea: Hà Nội through the seasons: hoa sữa in autumn, West Lake, and why Northerners say rét.

units.title: Question words
units.notes: thế nào is Northern (the South prefers sao or như thế nào). Bridges into the patterns phase.
units.storyIdea: Water puppetry, múa rối nước, and its narrator Chú Tễu.

units.title: Time and days
units.notes: muộn is Northern for late (the South says trễ). năm (year) was a warm-up gloss in lesson 2.
units.storyIdea: The lunar calendar and Tết, the twelve zodiac animals (a cat instead of the rabbit), and Quang Trung's surprise Tết victory at Đống Đa in 1789.

units.title: Places in the city
units.notes: phố and ga were contrast words in lesson 1; reuse that memory. Issue 13 (2026-11-27): quán, nhà, chợ, hồ with ... ở đâu?; the story is water puppetry (the questions unit's storyIdea), since the Old Quarter story was told in issue 9.
units.storyIdea: The 36 streets of the Old Quarter, each once named for its trade: Hàng Bạc (silver), Hàng Đồng (copper), Hàng Mã (paper offerings).

units.title: Weather and seasons in Hà Nội
units.notes: mây was a contrast word in lesson 2. nồm is the damp, sticky Hà Nội spring weather.
units.storyIdea: Nồm, mưa phùn and the Northern winter; Sơn Tinh and Thủy Tinh, the legend of the mountain god and the water god behind the floods.

units.title: Colours and clothes
units.notes: xanh covers blue and green; mũ is Northern for hat (the South says nón).
units.storyIdea: The áo dài and the conical hat (nón lá), and the silk village of Vạn Phúc.

units.title: The body and feeling unwell
units.notes: ốm is Northern for ill (the South says bệnh).
units.storyIdea: Lãn Ông, Hà Nội's traditional medicine street, named after an 18th-century physician.

clinics: Every fifth issue is a clinic built from leeches and mix-ups (docs/PEDAGOGY.md, Variety): issue 15 is the next one.
